A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-IN work, and their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. v2 retains v1's material and appends a largely duplicative supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP-IN classification, retrieval, compositional reasoning, MLLM and ablation results in Tables 1–7, plus feature visualizations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and repeats a subset in its appended supplement.

M1.justification: Both retain the same two-stage RoPE adaptation and distillation procedure, symmetric hard-negative loss, and combined short-caption/long-caption training objective in Sections 3.2–3.4.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation tasks are unchanged. Winoground, SugarCrepe and SPEC in the supplement already appear in v1 Section 4.4 and Table 3; they are not added benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments. In particular, DFN already appears in v1 Tables 1–2; the supplement repeats its comparisons alongside the existing CLIP variants.

E3.justification: Reported splits, metrics, sample counts, training settings and model configurations are retained. DFN ViT-H/14 evaluations at resolutions 224 and 378 already appear in v1, despite being described as additional experiments in the supplement.

E4.justification: The data-source, data-scale and component ablations in Tables 5–7 are unchanged. Supplementary Sections C–D repeat the instruction-editing examples and feature-activation analysis from v1 Appendices A–B.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The supplement continues the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 are retained. Supplementary Tables 1–3 reproduce existing results, including identical DFN and compositional-reasoning scores; the illustrated examples and feature maps also match.

T1.justification: The loss definitions and training objective in Equations 1–8 are mathematically unchanged. The appended supplement introduces no formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about instruction-editing negatives, long captions, RoPE adaptation, fine-grained perception and MLLM benefits.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section A adds a DFN-specific interpretation emphasizing transferability and consistent classification/retrieval improvement. The classification characterization overstates Table 1, which shows unchanged accuracy at 224 and a decline at 378. Existing compositional-reasoning and feature-map interpretations are repeated.

D1.justification: Caption generation, distillation details, hardware, optimizer, learning rate, weight decay, batch sizes and loss weights remain unchanged. The supplement supplies no additional implementation or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Both cite the same 56 works and retain the related-work discussion and novelty positioning. The supplement repeats the bibliography and discusses DFN, which was already cited and evaluated in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds a separately titled supplement with a roadmap, Sections A–D and another bibliography. Most supplementary prose repeats Section 4.4 and the original appendices; the original narrative and wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The original displays remain unchanged. The supplement repeats Tables 1–3, reverses the DFN/SigLIP2 block order in Tables 1–2, and redisplays Figures 3–4 as supplementary Figures 1–2, with separate pagination and line numbers.

improvement.justification: The new DFN discussion claims consistent classification improvement, although Table 1 in both versions shows 83.4% for both models at 224 and 84.4% baseline versus 84.1% CLIP-IN at 378. Any benefit from highlighting these results is outweighed by this inaccurate summary and the duplication of existing tables, figures and references. The decline in precision and organization is limited; the underlying study remains intact.
